html:
The Chukchi are a native people of the Chukotka Peninsula, the far northeastern tip of Siberia, facing Alaska across the Bering Strait. The map shows them from 1530 to 1700.

Like the Koryaks to their south, they had two ways of life. Reindeer Chukchi herded on the inland tundra. Maritime Chukchi lived on the coast, hunting walrus, seals and whales, alongside the Siberian Yupik. Coastal people traded across the strait with the peoples of Alaska long before Europeans came.

In 1648 the Cossack Semyon Dezhnyov sailed around their peninsula. In the 1700s Russia sent armed expeditions to force the Chukchi to pay tribute, and they fought back hard. Russia gave up conquest by force and turned to trade, so the Chukchi stayed only loosely under Russian rule into the 1800s, longer than most peoples of Siberia (Russian conquest of Siberia).
sum: The Chukchi are a native people of the Chukotka Peninsula, the far northeastern tip of Siberia, facing Alaska across the Bering Strait. The map shows them from 1530 to 1700.
